about.title: Personal Injury Help in Los Altos, California
about.longDescription: Los Altos may feel quiet compared to its neighbors, but public crash records show real activity on streets locals drive every day. In the most recent reporting year, the city logged 40 injury collisions, 43 injured people, and 1 traffic death. Corridors like Foothill Expressway, El Camino Real, I-280, and Fremont Avenue carry the bulk of local traffic and, with it, the bulk of recorded collisions. Reports also tend to cluster on Thursday mornings between 8 and 10 a.m., a pattern likely tied to commute and school-run traffic. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these incidents, sorting out medical care, insurance calls, and paperwork can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects injured people in Los Altos with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened. There's no cost to get connected, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. Reaching out costs you nothing and starts the process of getting real answers about your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before It's Too Late

items.title: Time Limits Apply
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your options.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Bar You
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault for the collision. Any compensation is simply adjusted to reflect your share of responsibility.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages in ordinary injury cases, meaning compensation for pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life isn't artificially capped like it is in some other states.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed and no fee unless you actually recover money.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Los Altos?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If the at-fault party is a government entity, such as the city or county, the notice period can be as short as six months, so it helps to act promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the crash?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do collisions tend to cluster in Los Altos?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along Foothill Expressway, El Camino Real, I-280, and Fremont Avenue, with reports also peaking on Thursday mornings between 8 and 10 a.m. These are neutral public-record patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is completely free, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney. We don't provide legal representation ourselves.
